scoring_note: Curated musical estimates on each 0-100 axis, not empirically calibrated listener results. Never infer a person's character from the songs. Valid tests require a >=20-point contrast.

songs.title: Good Life
songs.rationale: An exuberant vocal house announcement: immediate shared pleasure rather than introspective or dangerous dance music.

songs.title: Strings of Life
songs.rationale: A piano-led electronic instrumental that builds its own shared emotional trajectory without a singer explaining the feeling.

songs.title: French Kiss
songs.rationale: Its famous tempo disruption turns erotic house into a structural event; extraordinary gradual transformation against immediate anthems.

songs.title: Gypsy Woman (She's Homeless)
songs.rationale: A communal dance groove housing a social observation; music can feel euphoric while its story asks a difficult question.

songs.title: Show Me Love
songs.rationale: A direct, vocal-driven demand made for the dance floor, with little structural suspense or lyrical menace.

songs.title: Energy Flash
songs.rationale: Relentless, raw physical pressure with almost no comforting communal vocal; an ideal contrast to joyous house.

songs.title: The Bells
songs.rationale: A high-speed rhythmic alarm whose discipline and danger outweigh vocal intimacy or gradual revelation.

songs.title: Music Sounds Better with You
songs.rationale: A mirrorball loop that shares uncomplicated delight; the pleasure is polished, repetitive and collective.

songs.title: Praise You
songs.rationale: Messy sample charm and immediate movement; high shared warmth with deliberate rough edges.

songs.title: Brown Paper Bag
songs.rationale: Acoustic bass and breakbeat architecture unwind patiently; a compelling foil for harder, more immediate drum and bass.

songs.title: Higher State of Consciousness
songs.rationale: Acid repetition keeps ratcheting toward overload; high-pressure motion with more transformation than simple hook delivery.

songs.title: Lady (Hear Me Tonight)
songs.rationale: Effortless filtered disco romance, immediate and warm; ideal against a dangerous or distant machine-led groove.

songs.title: Groovejet (If This Ain't Love)
songs.rationale: Polished disco-house flirtation with instant gratification and almost no pressure; useful against cathartic EDM drama.

songs.title: Tarantula
songs.artist: Pendulum feat. DJ Fresh, $pyda & Tenor Fly
songs.rationale: A combustible jungle-influenced assault; measures appetite for rough impact against patient, atmospheric breaks.

songs.title: Pjanoo
songs.rationale: A crystalline piano motif carries collective euphoria with minimal menace, choosing momentum over long narrative uncertainty.

songs.title: An Ending (Ascent)
songs.rationale: Purely suspended ambient expanse with no rhythmic pressure; a defining slow-immersion and solitude anchor.

songs.title: Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites
songs.rationale: A violent timbral shape-shift with instant drops; separates raw rupture from polished melodic uplift.

songs.title: Promises
songs.rationale: A vocal confession riding dark, polished bass weight, balancing recognizable emotion and dance-floor tension.

songs.title: Latch
songs.rationale: Tight garage swing meets close-up romantic attachment, intimate despite being designed for communal dancing.

songs.title: Clarity
songs.rationale: Personal heartbreak magnified into festival catharsis; emotional exposure and enormous scale inhabit one track.

songs.title: Open Eye Signal
songs.rationale: A long, evolving mechanical journey that feels intense without asking the crowd to sing along.

songs.title: Cirrus
songs.rationale: A patient interlocking instrumental arrangement offers discovery and air rather than blunt impact.

songs.title: A Walk
songs.rationale: A sunlit instrumental landscape that moves but does not demand, ideal for separating atmosphere from force.

songs.title: Language
songs.rationale: An engineered ascent toward a luminous collective release; gradual payoff with very low darkness.

songs.title: Loud Places
songs.rationale: A tender, sampled club memory swells into shared voices, private heartbreak made communal.

songs.title: Innerbloom
songs.rationale: An epic patient build rooted in an intimate human confession, testing the willingness to wait for transformation.

songs.title: Losing It
songs.rationale: The point is the drop, now; an almost pure high-impact public dance-floor payoff with scant narrative development.

songs.title: A Moment Apart
songs.rationale: Orchestral-electronic uplift on a cinematic scale, a generous slow reveal rather than raw club danger.

songs.title: Emerald Rush
songs.rationale: A severe yet meticulously designed rhythmic build: menace and transformation without a conventional singalong.

songs.title: Marea (We've Lost Dancing)
songs.rationale: A collective dance anthem built around absence and return; communal hope without overconfident celebration.

songs.title: Delilah (pull me out of this)
songs.rationale: Vocal fragments become urgent rhythmic release, where a personal plea is transformed into a club-wide shout.

songs.title: B.O.T.A. (Baddest of Them All)
songs.rationale: Cheeky, immediate bassline house with unmistakable communal intent; pleasure without existential stakes.

songs.title: Rumble
songs.rationale: A spare but punishing modern bass threat, more confrontational rhythm than melodic invitation.

songs.title: Where You Are
songs.rationale: The love-song hook is projected at festival scale, polished and collectively cathartic.

songs.title: Baddy on the Floor
songs.rationale: A mischievous dance-floor invitation, all playful release and little menace, with a sampled disco-house smile.

songs.title: Move
songs.rationale: Afro-house momentum opens gradually into a shared groove, a patient spell rather than a hard drop.

songs.title: On My Knees
songs.rationale: A vulnerable plea suspended over a dark melodic house build, big in sound while emotionally exposed.

pairings.phrase: Sing the future, or build it from machines?
pairings.why: Inner City gives the room immediate vocal joy; Derrick May builds a patient, rawer instrumental emotional landscape.

pairings.phrase: Invite everyone in, or see how much pressure the room can take?
pairings.why: Good Life makes the club welcoming and bright; Energy Flash strips it to threatening mechanical force.

pairings.phrase: Build a future for a crowd, or drift beyond the clock entirely?
pairings.why: Rhythim Is Rhythim makes a dance floor out of evolving piano; Brian Eno removes rhythm, threat and public address.

pairings.phrase: Make the machine feel human, or let the acid take over?
pairings.why: Lil Louis turns a house record into bodily drama; Josh Wink projects impersonal acid pressure outward.

pairings.phrase: Let the track make you wait, or let the chorus deliver?
pairings.why: French Kiss manipulates time and expectation; Robin S. offers an upfront vocal house declaration.

pairings.phrase: Hear the story under the beat, or just believe in the hook?
pairings.why: Crystal Waters folds social observation into vocal house; Robin S. keeps the emotional invitation direct and affirming.

pairings.phrase: Who's being left behind, or who's coming home with you?
pairings.why: Gypsy Woman's communal hook carries a difficult observation; Modjo's filtered groove is low-pressure romance.

pairings.phrase: Take the punch now, or wait while the acid coils?
pairings.why: Joey Beltram hits hard without a long arc; Josh Wink builds toward a broader communal overload.

pairings.phrase: The alarm that never blinks, or a rhythm that keeps discovering rooms?
pairings.why: Jeff Mills maintains relentless threat; Roni Size offers air, detail and gradual breakbeat changes.

pairings.phrase: A hard private machine, or a drop the whole room owns?
pairings.why: The Bells is raw, severe and functional; Losing It turns tech-house impact into a polished group release.

pairings.phrase: Perfect mirrorball, or crate-digging grin?
pairings.why: Stardust sounds lacquered and precisely looped; Fatboy Slim makes delight feel scrappy and sampled.

pairings.phrase: Pure disco glaze, or a house song with bruises?
pairings.why: Stardust offers an untroubled surface; Crystal Waters threads observation and social unease through the dance groove.

pairings.phrase: A sampled wink, or a maze of bass?
pairings.why: Fatboy Slim creates instant communal levity; Roni Size rewards solitary attention to a longer instrumental design.

pairings.phrase: Let the breaks breathe, or throw them at the wall?
pairings.why: Roni Size makes a patient, textured drum-and-bass journey; Pendulum supplies abrasive immediate impact.

pairings.phrase: Acid for the masses, or a storm you enter alone?
pairings.why: Josh Wink projects collective squelch and raw force; Jon Hopkins turns rhythmic menace into a private, refined environment.

pairings.phrase: Stay on the disco floor, or turn heartbreak into fireworks?
pairings.why: Spiller keeps pleasure local, steady and assured; Zedd magnifies a vulnerable feeling into an EDM climax.

pairings.phrase: Take the sledgehammer, or wait for the machine to change weapons?
pairings.why: Pendulum maintains a punishing DnB rush; Skrillex's dubstep keeps mutating its timbral attack.

pairings.phrase: Ride the bright riff, or wait for the sky to open?
pairings.why: Pjanoo is propelled by an instantly recognizable piano; Language makes a longer emotional ascent.

pairings.phrase: Disappear into the air, or move gently through the landscape?
pairings.why: Eno suspends the clock almost entirely; Tycho keeps a soft but definite rhythmic journey moving.

pairings.phrase: A room for nobody, or a room we have to rebuild together?
pairings.why: Eno's ambient solitude contrasts with Fred again.. and The Blessed Madonna's explicitly collective club remembrance.

pairings.phrase: Corrupted machine, or soaring confession?
pairings.why: Skrillex uses raw, alien drops; Nero sets heavy bass around a polished human vocal.

pairings.phrase: Love with teeth, or heartbreak with a parachute?
pairings.why: Nero's melodic bass carries a darker pressure; Clarity pushes the same feeling toward festival catharsis.

pairings.phrase: Dance close to one person, or sing to an entire stadium?
pairings.why: Disclosure's garage hook stays compact and intimate; Zedd increases scale and dramatic payoff.

pairings.phrase: Lock the groove, or let the memory swell?
pairings.why: Latch holds a close rhythmic shape; Loud Places changes from private recollection into a broader shared chorus.

pairings.phrase: Take the storm head-on, or let the clouds pass over you?
pairings.why: Jon Hopkins imposes insistent mechanical pressure; Bonobo lets an intricate journey breathe more easily.

pairings.phrase: A clockwork journey, or a place you could stay forever?
pairings.why: Bonobo's pieces keep changing and tightening; Tycho prioritizes serene atmospheric continuity.

pairings.phrase: Walk through the landscape, or fall inside the singer's head?
pairings.why: Tycho gives distance and air; RÜFÜS DU SOL sets a long, large-scale inward confession in motion.

pairings.phrase: A sky-sized release, or a long private ache?
pairings.why: Porter Robinson gives the crowd a hopeful payoff; Innerbloom delays gratification inside vulnerable feeling.

pairings.phrase: An old dance-floor memory, or a new one we lost?
pairings.why: Jamie xx wraps nostalgia in polish; Marea leaves the shared yearning more exposed and rough-edged.

pairings.phrase: Six minutes of private confession, or hands-up certainty?
pairings.why: Innerbloom is patient and inward; John Summit and HAYLA make an enormous immediate communal declaration.

pairings.phrase: The drop hits, or someone's voice breaks through?
pairings.why: FISHER treats the drop as the point; Fred again.. turns a sampled plea into a changing rhythmic story.

pairings.phrase: Weaponized bassline, or cheeky invitation?
pairings.why: Losing It's impersonal pressure contrasts with the more vocal and easygoing B.O.T.A.

pairings.phrase: Cinematic uplift, or a controlled collision?
pairings.why: ODESZA designs a broad, polished welcome; Jon Hopkins keeps threat and private intensity inside the machinery.

pairings.phrase: Watch the machine evolve, or release the beast in ten seconds?
pairings.why: Emerald Rush earns its force through gradual construction; Rumble uses immediate raw bass confrontation.

pairings.phrase: Mourn the lost room, or just throw the doors open?
pairings.why: Marea makes the club an emotional memory; B.O.T.A. brings an instant, confident communal hook.

pairings.phrase: Let the sample become longing, or hit a hook that never looks back?
pairings.why: Delilah keeps changing its vocal urgency; B.O.T.A. holds an easy pleasure principle with less friction.

pairings.phrase: Bass like a threat, or a chorus like a rescue flare?
pairings.why: Skrillex and Flowdan prioritize raw menace; John Summit gives the crowd polished melodic assurance.

pairings.phrase: A chorus for everyone, or a confession you can barely stand?
pairings.why: Where You Are is a confident festival-scale reunion; On My Knees exposes vulnerability over a slower dark build.

pairings.phrase: Instant disco wink, or a slow spell you fall under?
pairings.why: Jamie xx and Honey Dijon put their invitation up front; Adam Port and Stryv let the groove unfold more patiently.

pairings.phrase: Hands raised in joy, or hands raised because they're needed?
pairings.why: Move sounds secure and celebratory; Marea mixes shared yearning with an unsettled memory.

pairings.phrase: Stretch the vulnerable plea across a whole night, or let a sample cut straight through?
pairings.why: RÜFÜS DU SOL slowly exposes the feeling in polished darkness; Fred again.. turns vulnerability into urgent rhythmic command.

pairings.phrase: Coil the future slowly, or open the rave gates?
pairings.why: Derrick May's raw, emotional techno unfolds; Orbital's Chime brings a brighter, more immediate group invitation.

pairings.phrase: Alone in orbit, or telling somebody about the clouds?
pairings.why: Brian Eno removes human contact and beat; The Orb creates a spoken, approachable psychedelic space.

pairings.phrase: Piano hook now, or nine minutes before the sky opens?
pairings.why: Pjanoo makes its joyful motif immediate; Strobe earns its climax slowly with more dramatic tension.

pairings.phrase: A computer learning to scream, or a human starting the fire?
pairings.why: Skrillex turns rapid digital transformations outward; The Prodigy's Firestarter puts a human threat at the center.

pairings.phrase: An anthem mourning the club, or one that refuses to close?
pairings.why: Marea waits within a rough-edged communal memory; Daft Punk delivers immaculate immediate celebration.

pairings.phrase: Stand alone inside the machine, or hear a ghost inside it?
pairings.why: Hopkins brings propulsion and abstraction at scale; Burial's Archangel places a wounded voice in a smaller, shadowed room.

pairings.phrase: A memory you can sing, or a memory you can only dance?
pairings.why: Jamie xx makes past love immediate and personal; Bicep's Glue observes nostalgia from a more distant instrumental viewpoint.

pairings.phrase: A human confession inside a long build, or the beauty of a machine ascending?
pairings.why: Innerbloom puts vulnerability into an unfolding song; Strobe makes the long ascent more abstract and commanding.

pairings.phrase: Vocal-house mischief, or a neon robot dance class?
pairings.why: Jamie xx warms an old-school invitation; Justice's D.A.N.C.E. watches the club through a crisp, playful machine.

pairings.phrase: The crowd becomes the beat, or the beat leaves the crowd behind?
pairings.why: Move coaxes shared physical momentum; 808 State's Pacific State is a spacious, distant instrumental drift.

pairings.phrase: Disco champagne, or metal shutters coming down?
pairings.why: Groovejet is polished flirtatious release; Rumble makes an impersonal, raw threat out of bass music.
